claim_being_audited: The Actor claims the current release can be certified as model-card compliant and evidentially supported despite a current insurance-claims-triage subgroup regression, based on aggregate readiness evidence plus release documentation that would frame the subgroup weakness as a material limitation.
decision_criteria: Certification is compliant only if current release documentation reflects current evaluation results.
Material weaknesses for named launch use cases must be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved mitigation before launch.
Aggregate readiness and lack of severity-one rehearsal incidents support overall readiness but do not waive the disclosure/mitigation requirement.
Prior approvals and informal monitoring may inform context but cannot substitute for current-release evidence or reviewed acceptance.
evidence_requests: Provide the current release model-card or equivalent release documentation showing the insurance-claims-triage regression is explicitly disclosed as a material limitation.
Provide approved risk acceptance or reviewed mitigation covering this named launch use case if disclosure is not the chosen path.
Provide evidence that the certification decision was made after the current retrieval configuration change and current evaluation batch were incorporated into release documentation.
specific_concerns: The admissible record shows a current subgroup weakness for a named launch use case.
The policy requires material segment weaknesses to be disclosed or covered by approved mitigation before certification may proceed.
The file contains no attached disclosure language, approved mitigation, or approved risk acceptance for the current release.
Prior approval and informal post-launch monitoring are explicitly insufficient substitutes under the policy text.
unsupported_claims: That certification can proceed now on the present record.
That current release documentation already reflects the subgroup regression as required by policy.
That informal monitoring and prior approval are enough to close the disclosure/mitigation predicate for this release.
